# systemd in Stage 1: the 26.05 Initrd Default

**Goal:** Know what changed when NixOS 26.05 made the **systemd-based initrd** the default for stage 1. Move old `boot.initrd.*Commands` shell hooks into real initrd units, and catch the two migration traps that evaluation *cannot* catch for you (`/dev/root` and LUKS device timeouts). The scripted stage 1 still exists behind `boot.initrd.systemd.enable = false`, but it is deprecated and **scheduled for removal in 26.11**. Treat this chapter as an upgrade item for this release cycle, not a someday item.

Version note: everything below was evaluated against **nixos-26.05** (`26.05.20261010.6fcc160`) with **Nix 2.35.3**. All evaluation output is pasted from those runs. The initrd's systemd is **260.5** on this channel.

## Mental model

Stage 1 is the small root filesystem the kernel unpacks from the initrd. It has one job: find the real root, mount it at `/sysroot`, and hand over to stage 2 (the system you log into). NixOS has had two implementations of that job:

```text
scripted stage 1 (≤ 25.11 default)          systemd stage 1 (26.05 default)
───────────────────────────────────         ─────────────────────────────────────────
/init = one generated bash script           /init = systemd, PID 1 in the initrd
  preLVMCommands                              units ordered by bootup(7):
  preDeviceCommands                             systemd-udevd → cryptsetup → *.device
  postDeviceCommands      ◀── your hooks        → sysroot.mount → initrd-fs.target
  postMountCommands           are spliced       → initrd-nixos-activation
  (switch_root by hand)       into the script   → initrd-switch-root
                                              your code = boot.initrd.systemd.services.*
```

The scripted initrd ran your strings *in sequence* inside one script. The systemd initrd has no sequence. It has a **dependency graph**, and your code becomes a unit with `Before=` / `After=` edges inside that graph. Most migration work is choosing the right edge.

## Worked examples

The lab is one flake with several host variants. None of them is booted. Every case is proved at evaluation time, which is where NixOS reports most of its stage-1 decisions.

```nix
# flake.nix — minimal host to inspect the stage-1 initrd that nixos-26.05 builds
{
  inputs.nixpkgs.url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixos-26.05";
  outputs = { nixpkgs, ... }: {
    nixosConfigurations.box = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem {
      modules = [ ./host.nix ];
    };
    nixosConfigurations.trap = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem { modules = [ ./host.nix ./trap-scripted.nix ]; };
    nixosConfigurations.fixed = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem { modules = [ ./host.nix ./initrd-service.nix ]; };
    nixosConfigurations.devroot = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem { modules = [ ./host.nix ./trap-devroot.nix ]; };
    nixosConfigurations.scripted = nixpkgs.lib.nixosSystem { modules = [ ./host.nix ./opt-out.nix ]; };
  };
}
```

```nix
# host.nix — the smallest bootable-looking host; nothing about initrd is set here
{ ... }: {
  nixpkgs.hostPlatform = "x86_64-linux";
  boot.loader.systemd-boot.enable = true;
  fileSystems."/" = { device = "/dev/disk/by-label/nixos"; fsType = "ext4"; };
  system.stateVersion = "26.05";
}
```

### Case 1: Confirm what you are running

Do not assume the default from memory. Ask the configuration:

```console
$ nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.box.config.system.nixos.label
"26.05.20261010.6fcc160"
$ nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.box.config.boot.initrd.systemd.enable
true
$ nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.box.config.boot.initrd.systemd.services --apply builtins.attrNames
[ "dbus" "initrd-find-nixos-closure" "initrd-nixos-activation" "initrd-parse-etc" "initrd-switch-root" "modprobe@" "panic-on-fail" "systemd-tmpfiles-setup" "systemd-tmpfiles-setup-sysroot" ]
```

The `initrd-*` services are the NixOS-specific part. They locate the system closure on the new root, run activation against `/sysroot`, and switch root. Everything else in the boot is upstream systemd behaviour, as documented in `bootup(7)`, and that is the point of the change. Mounting, LUKS prompts, udev and timeouts now follow the same rules as on any systemd distribution.

### Case 2: An old hook fails evaluation (the good failure)

A config written for the scripted initrd often carries a hook like this:

```nix
# trap-scripted.nix — a scripted-stage-1 hook carried over from an older config
{ ... }: {
  boot.initrd.postDeviceCommands = ''
    echo "waiting for slow disk"; sleep 2
  '';
}
```

On 26.05 it does not silently vanish. It stops the build:

```console
$ nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.trap.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath
error:
Failed assertions:
- systemd stage 1 does not support `boot.initrd.postDeviceCommands`. Instead, create systemd services using the `boot.initrd.systemd.services` options, which has an API matching the stage 2 `systemd.services` options. Refer to `bootup(7)`, specifically the sections on "Bootup in the Initrd" and "System Manager Bootup", for information about when various units happen, and order services accordingly.

    Definitions:
    - /nix/store/…-source/trap-scripted.nix
```

The same assertion covers `preFailCommands`, `preDeviceCommands`, `preLVMCommands`, `postDeviceCommands` and `postMountCommands`. Grep for all of them before you upgrade:

```console
$ grep -rnE 'boot\.initrd\.(preFail|preDevice|preLVM|postDevice|postMount)Commands' /etc/nixos
```

### Case 3: Rewrite the hook as an initrd unit

The replacement uses the stage-2 `systemd.services` API under `boot.initrd.systemd.services`. The work is choosing edges. "After devices, before root is mounted" becomes `Before=sysroot.mount`:

```nix
# initrd-service.nix — the same hook as a real unit inside the systemd initrd
{ pkgs, ... }: {
  boot.initrd.systemd.services.slow-disk-settle = {
    description = "Give the slow disk two seconds before root is mounted";
    wantedBy = [ "initrd.target" ];
    before = [ "sysroot.mount" ];
    after = [ "systemd-udev-settle.service" ];
    unitConfig.DefaultDependencies = false;
    serviceConfig.Type = "oneshot";
    script = ''
      echo "waiting for slow disk"; sleep 2
    '';
  };
}
```

Read back the unit NixOS will put into the initrd:

```console
$ nix eval --raw '.#nixosConfigurations.fixed.config.boot.initrd.systemd.units."slow-disk-settle.service".text'
[Unit]
After=systemd-udev-settle.service
Before=sysroot.mount
DefaultDependencies=false
Description=Give the slow disk two seconds before root is mounted

[Service]
Environment="LOCALE_ARCHIVE=/nix/store/dc427sjs…-glibc-locales-2.42-100/lib/locale/locale-archive"
Environment="TZDIR=/nix/store/mkbbamyc…-tzdata-2026c/share/zoneinfo"
ExecStart=/nix/store/yb7a6i88…-unit-script-slow-disk-settle-start/bin/slow-disk-settle-start
Type=oneshot

[Install]
WantedBy=initrd.target
```

Two facts make this safe. First, the generated script is copied into the initrd automatically. Second, `sleep` resolves, because coreutils is in the initrd's default `PATH`:

```console
$ nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.fixed.config.boot.initrd.systemd.storePaths \
    --apply 'ps: builtins.filter (p: builtins.match ".*slow-disk.*" (toString (p.source or p)) != null) ps'
[ { dlopen = { features = [ ]; usePriority = "recommended"; }; enable = true; source = "/nix/store/yb7a6i88…-unit-script-slow-disk-settle-start/bin/slow-disk-settle-start"; target = null; } ]
$ nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.fixed.config.boot.initrd.systemd.initrdBin --apply 'map (p: p.name)'
[ "lvm2-2.03.39" "e2fsprogs-1.47.4" "coreutils-9.11" "systemd-260.5" "kmod-31" "bash-interactive-5.3p9" ]
```

Any *other* binary your hook calls must be listed in `boot.initrd.systemd.initrdBin` (on `PATH`) or `boot.initrd.systemd.storePaths` (copied only). The initrd is not your system closure.

`DefaultDependencies=false` matters. Without it, systemd adds `After=sysinit.target basic.target` and the implicit shutdown conflicts. In the initrd those can create an ordering cycle with mounts that `basic.target` waits for. Early-boot units almost always want it off.

### Case 4: The trap evaluation will not catch: `/dev/root`

The scripted initrd created a `/dev/root` symlink from `root=` on the kernel command line. The systemd initrd does not. A config that names it still evaluates cleanly:

```nix
# trap-devroot.nix — a root filesystem named by the scripted-initrd symlink
{ lib, ... }: { fileSystems."/".device = lib.mkForce "/dev/root"; }
```

```console
$ nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.devroot.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath
"/nix/store/nc5n9p8y…-nixos-system-nixos-26.05.20261010.6fcc160.drv"
```

No warning and no assertion, and on the next boot `sysroot.mount` waits for a device that never appears. Name the root with `/dev/disk/by-label/…`, `/dev/disk/by-uuid/…` or `/dev/mapper/…`, then check:

```console
$ nix eval --json .#nixosConfigurations.box.config.fileSystems --apply 'fs: builtins.mapAttrs (_: v: v.device) fs'
{"/":"/dev/disk/by-label/nixos"}
```

The LUKS case is in the same family. The release notes say `fileSystems."/".device` should be `/dev/mapper/<name>`, matching `boot.initrd.luks.devices.<name>`. Otherwise systemd's default device timeout can expire while you are still typing the passphrase. For LVM on LUKS, add `"x-systemd.device-timeout=infinity"` to the root's `options`. If you are already locked out, `systemd.default_device_timeout_sec=infinity` on the kernel command line gets you in.

### Case 5: The escape hatch, and its warning

```nix
# opt-out.nix — reverting to the scripted stage 1 (deprecated on 26.05)
{ ... }: { boot.initrd.systemd.enable = false; }
```

```console
$ nix eval .#nixosConfigurations.scripted.config.system.build.toplevel.drvPath
evaluation warning: Scripted initrd is deprecated and scheduled for removal in 26.11. See the NixOS 26.05 release notes.
"/nix/store/cr5jdspc…-nixos-system-nixos-26.05.20261010.6fcc160.drv"
```

Use it to get a machine booting tonight. Do not use it as a destination. If you keep it, give the line a dated comment and open an issue to remove it before you move to 26.11.

## The trap

The dangerous migrations are the ones that **evaluate fine**. Hooks fail loudly (Case 2), and that is the easy part. `/dev/root`, a LUKS root named by UUID instead of `/dev/mapper/<name>`, and remote unlock scripts that call `cryptsetup-askpass` all build successfully and fail at the console. (`cryptsetup-askpass` no longer exists. Use `systemctl default`, and `ssh -o RequestTTY=force` if you pipe the passphrase over SSH.) Your rollback is the previous generation in the boot menu, so keep it until the new initrd has booted at least once *on that hardware*.

## The boring rule

Before switching a host to 26.05: grep for `*Commands` hooks and port them to `boot.initrd.systemd.services` with explicit `Before=`/`After=` and `DefaultDependencies=false`. Name every root and LUKS device by a stable path. Boot once with the old generation still in the menu. Do not ship `boot.initrd.systemd.enable = false` without a removal date.

## Try this

1. Change Case 3 to `before = [ "initrd-root-device.target" ]` and read the unit again. Which `bootup(7)` milestone does that correspond to, and does it still run before `sysroot.mount`?
2. Add `pkgs.util-linux` to `boot.initrd.systemd.initrdBin`, call `blkid` from the hook, and confirm the binary appears in the initrd's `PATH`.
3. Build `config.system.build.initialRamdisk` for `box` and `scripted` and compare their sizes with `du -h`.
4. In a NixOS VM test (`nixosTest`), boot `fixed` and grep `journalctl -b -u slow-disk-settle` from the test script.
